the development and application of a method for the quantitative determination of total flavonoids in cranberry juice.

the effect of cranberry extract on the activities of the antioxidant enzymes in liver and lung tissues of obese and nonobese mice, and the possible role played by the antioxidant enzymes in the development of obesity.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

cranberry extract-enrichment of the diet of obese mice increases NQO1 and CAT activities in the liver and kidneys, whereas in nonobese counterparts, no significant changes were detected in NQO1 or CAT activities.
the cranberry diet is not effective in the treatment of obesity.
cranberry extract is effective in decreasing body weight, fat mass, and fat cell size in obese mice, and in increasing NQO1 and CAT activities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cranberry extract-enrichment of the diets of obese but not of nonobese mice increases the activities of the antioxidant enzymes NAD(P) H:quinone oxidorenductase and catalaase.
the use of cranberry extract-enrichment in diet can be a useful strategy to reduce the risk of developing cancer in obese mice.
the consumption of cranberries and cranberry extracts may have beneficial effects on the antioxidant defense system of the body and on the detoxification system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cranberry is not a superfood and should not be considered a health supplement.
cranberry extract-enrichment of a high-fat diet can reduce obesity and improve metabolic syndrome by increasing the activity of antioxidant enzymes and by reducing oxidative stress.
a diet rich in cranberries can improve metabolic health in obese mice by increasing antioxidant defenses and reducing oxidative stress.
